title: Scale-Aware Adaptive Supervised Network with Limited Medical Annotations
core_idea: Introduce SASNet, a dual-branch architecture that fuses low-level and high-level features via novel scale-aware adaptive reweighting to handle limited annotations. Key components are: (1) a scale-aware adaptive reweight strategy that dynamically weights pixel-wise predictions using temporal confidence accumulation, (2) a view variance enhancement mechanism using 3D Fourier-domain transformations to simulate annotation variability, and (3) segmentation–regression consistency learning with signed distance maps to improve boundary precision. These components integrate spatial, temporal, and geometric consistency within a unified optimization framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation.
tldr: A semi-supervised segmentation framework (SASNet) that combines scale-aware adaptive reweighting, simulated annotation variability in the 3D Fourier domain, and signed distance map consistency to better handle annotation scarcity, inter-annotator variability, and multi-scale boundary delineation.
